alternatives.root_cause: checkout itself exhausted a local resource (connection pool, threads, or heap causing GC thrash), so requests queued inside checkout rather than in any dependency.
alternatives.why_not: Pure exhaustion usually escalates into errors (timeouts, 5xx) and pulls frontend/frontend-proxy into alerting too; here only a latency warning on checkout is reported.

alternatives.root_cause: A checkout-only dependency's process was stopped while its socket still accepted, so checkout hung to its deadlines on every order.
alternatives.why_not: A full freeze would normally drive checkout past its timeouts into an error alert, not a latency warning, and would likely take frontend down with it.

verdict.summary: checkout's end-to-end latency rose because one of its synchronous downstream calls (most plausibly a checkout-only dependency such as payment, currency, email or shipping) became slow, and checkout blocked on it while holding request threads.
verdict.reasoning: The only alert is a latency warning on checkout, with no error alerts anywhere and no second service alerting. checkout is the deepest fan-out node in this graph (product-catalog, currency, cart, email, payment, shipping), so it is the natural place for a downstream slowdown to surface first; the listed blast radius is just graph traversal from checkout, not independent evidence. If product-catalog or cart were the slow dependency I would expect frontend/recommendation to degrade too, so a checkout-exclusive dependency (payment, currency, email, shipping) is the more likely source — a slow dependency that is merely latent, not erroring, would not alert on its own. Latency with no errors and no restart-worthy symptom argues against a bad artifact or a wrong config value, which usually fail fast and loudly.
